answer: Sybil resistance rests on a stake bond escrowed on-chain for every identity. To bid on work, a new agent must lock tokens first, and payouts unlock on a schedule. One upheld fraud claim lets witnesses slash the entire bond. An attacker running a hollow swarm of clones must therefore post that lock for each clone, and a juniper cluster of fake agents earns nothing until it risks real capital. Creating ten thousand identities costs ten thousand locks, and a single whisper of collusion forfeits all of them. Faking identity stays expensive; verifying it stays cheap.
